CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ankle injury sustained during basketball game.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
45-year-old male presents with right ankle injury sustained today while playing basketball with his son at the courts. Patient went up for a shot and was contacted by his son while in the air. Upon landing, patient landed awkwardly, rolled and twisted his ankle. Patient reports pain primarily on the outside of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. Patient notes difficulty walking and reports the ankle does not feel stable or solid. Patient recently returned to a consistent workout routine at the gym and is concerned about disrupting his progress. Patient also notes he recently volunteered to coach basketball starting in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No other complaints noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not documented.

MEDICATIONS
No current medications listed.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Son Sean, age 10, plays basketball.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works from home. Recently returned to regular gym workouts. Plays recreational basketball with son. Has dogs at home. Volunteered to coach basketball starting in April.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right ankle with visible swelling and bruising on lateral side. Exquisite tenderness to palpation over lateral ankle. Tenderness noted over medial deltoid region. Skin intact with brisk capillary refill. No malalignment noted. Patient able to stand but reports difficulty walking due to pain and instability.

RESULTS
X-ray of right ankle (AP, lateral, and oblique views): Displaced lateral malleolus fracture at Weber C level. No evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures. Findings consistent with unstable ankle fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right ankle lateral malleolar fracture, Weber C. Surgical intervention recommended with plate and screw fixation. Patient will require crutches and approximately 3 months recovery time. Meloxicam prescribed for pain and swelling management. Patient instructed to ice ankle and maintain elevation, which is feasible given work-from-home status. Plan to return to activity and coaching within 3-month timeframe.
